name: Claude Code (usage telemetry)

name: Codex (built-in analytics)
versionScope: Official analytics.enabled contract checked 2026-11-21. The unset default depends on the client. TOML, profile overrides, managed requirements and custom CODEX_HOME are not evaluated; the standard config file is detection evidence only, so even a saved opt-out remains unknown. analytics.enabled=false disables built-in analytics, not custom OTLP exporters, feedback or model-service traffic. Settings and installed-version applicability require manual confirmation. Config location: https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-basic

actions.instruction: Confirm your client version and active config/profile: set [analytics] enabled = false in the effective config.toml (normally ~/.codex/config.toml, or CODEX_HOME/config.toml). This controls built-in analytics; custom OTLP metrics require otel.metrics_exporter = "none" separately. Review configured log/trace exporters and feedback separately.

name: Gemini CLI (usage statistics)
versionScope: Official configuration reference checked 2026-11-21: the nested privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled schema dates from v0.3.0. Its documented default is true, but the installed schema version, authentication mode and higher-priority system/project settings are not established by this probe. The user file is detection evidence only; report unknown even for a saved false value. This usage-statistics control is separate from OpenTelemetry export: https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/telemetry/

actions.instruction: Confirm the installed version uses the nested settings schema, then set privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled to false in ~/.gemini/settings.json and restart Gemini CLI. Check overriding system/project settings. This controls usage statistics; OpenTelemetry export is configured separately via telemetry.enabled or GEMINI_TELEMETRY_ENABLED.

name: GitHub CLI (core telemetry)

GitHub Enterprise Server targets are excluded from collection. This covers core gh only, excluding extensions and Copilot. actions.instruction: Confirm the installed version and active profile/user settings, then set telemetry.telemetryLevel to "off" in VS Code Settings (JSON). Check managed policy with your administrator. This disables product telemetry; independent extensions need their own controls.

Review Nx Console extension telemetry and Nx Cloud controls separately; NX_DAEMON=false and NX_NO_CLOUD=true do not establish that CLI usage analytics is disabled.

actions.instruction: Confirm this is Yarn Modern (v2+), rather than Yarn Classic or Hadoop YARN. In the intended Modern Yarn environment, run yarn config set --home enableTelemetry 0, then review the effective version, rc filename and project/environment overrides. User YAML can contain registry credentials and is not read by this scanner.

actions.instruction: Open Zed Settings and search for telemetry. Set both telemetry.metrics = false and telemetry.diagnostics = false in the effective settings. These controls cover client-side metrics and crash reports; required metadata for hosted services such as AI and Collaboration is separate.

name: PowerShell (pwsh telemetry)
versionScope: Official PowerShell telemetry contract checked 2026-11-21. This rule detects pwsh, not the separate Windows PowerShell powershell executable. POWERSHELL_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT must be set before starting the process and covers startup and session telemetry; 1, true and yes are documented opt-out values. Without this override, installed version/build and effective settings are unknown: PowerShell 7.6.2+ on Windows can also respect Windows optional diagnostic-data settings, which this tool rule does not use to infer PowerShell state. name: Go toolchain (telemetry collection and uploads)
versionScope: Official Go telemetry contract checked 2026-11-21. Go 1.23+ provides go telemetry off to disable both local collection and uploading. The local mode keeps counters locally without uploading; it is not complete opt-out. GOTELEMETRY and GOTELEMETRYDIR are read-only go env outputs, not environment overrides. A PATH-visible go does not establish the version or saved mode; the plain-text mode store is outside the JSON/JSONC setting parser and is not read or used for detection. Defaults and settings therefore remain unknown. The command is suggested only as a version-qualified manual step, never executed. This scope includes participating Go-maintained toolchain programs, not arbitrary applications written in Go.

actions.instruction: Confirm the active toolchain is Go 1.23 or later, then run go telemetry off to disable both local collection and uploading. The local mode only prevents uploads. GOTELEMETRY is read-only go env output; exporting GOTELEMETRY=off does not configure telemetry. For older toolchains, follow the official gotelemetry instructions and verify the applicable tools.

name: dbt (CLI anonymous usage statistics)

Current documentation distinguishes DBT_SEND_ANONYMOUS_USAGE_STATS for v1 through 1.10 and DBT_ENGINE_SEND_ANONYMOUS_USAGE_STATS for v1 1.11+ and v2, and documents DO_NOT_TRACK=1 for maintained versions. actions.instruction: Confirm the active dbt engine and version. For v1 through 1.10 use DBT_SEND_ANONYMOUS_USAGE_STATS=false; for v1 1.11+ or v2 use DBT_ENGINE_SEND_ANONYMOUS_USAGE_STATS=false. Current documentation also supports DO_NOT_TRACK=1. Verify effective invocation flags and version support. Database credentials in profiles.yml and project files are not read; hosted-platform and adapter telemetry are separate.
